instructions: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into 1/2 inch cubes. That should be about 4 cups. Dice the onion and the bell pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Add the turkey, press it into an even layer, and sprinkle it with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the 1 tsp garlic powder. Don't stir it. Leave it for about 3 minutes, until the underside is browned.

Add the onion and bell pepper. Break the turkey up with a wooden spoon and cook, stirring now and then, for 4 to 5 minutes, until there's no pink left and the onion is soft. Transfer everything to a bowl.
Add 1 tbsp of the oil to the same pan over medium heat. Add the sweet potatoes and 1/2 tsp of the salt and stir to coat them. Leave them for about 3 minutes, until the undersides start to brown.

Pour in 1/4 cup water and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cover, turn the heat to medium low and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring once or twice, until a fork slides easily into a cube. If the pan goes dry, add a splash of water.

Meanwhile, make the chipotle sauce. Mince the garlic clove and 1 of the chipotle peppers. Squeeze the lime. That should be about 2 tbsp juice. Whisk the garlic, chipotle, lime juice, 2 tsp honey, the remaining 2 tbsp oil, the last 1/4 tsp salt and the pinch of pepper together in a small bowl.
Uncover the pan and turn the heat to medium. Add the turkey and vegetables back in with 2 cups of the spinach. Stir for about 1 minute, until the spinach has wilted and the turkey is hot.
Take the pan off the heat. Scatter 1/2 cup of the mozzarella over the top, cover, and leave it for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the chipotle sauce on the side.
method_notes: All three brown a pound of ground turkey, cook diced sweet potato covered with a little liquid until tender and finish with cheese, in about 30 minutes. Real Food Whole Life (the lead) browns the turkey first, cooks the potatoes in the same pan with water, then brings it together with spinach, a chipotle honey lime sauce and cheese; Primavera Kitchen and Bucket List Tummy add onion and bell pepper, which this version cooks with the turkey. The lead stirs half the chipotle sauce into the pan; here it all goes on the side so the skillet stays mild. No version had 20 ratings at 4.0 or better (Primavera's has 1,558 at 3.6) and RecipeTin Eats has no version, so the top rated version read leads.
